title.en: Single cell protein and plant tissue culture

hook.en: About a quarter of a kilogram of a fast-growing bacterium, given cheap methanol and air, can in principle make tonnes of protein a day. Meanwhile, a single tiny piece of a banana plant can give thousands of identical plantlets in a lab.

objectives.en: Describe plant tissue culture and micropropagation

narration.en: About a quarter of a kilogram of a fast-growing bacterium, given cheap methanol and air, can in principle make tonnes of protein a day. Meanwhile, a single tiny piece of a banana plant can give thousands of identical plantlets in a lab.

body.en: Growing enough meat and milk takes a lot of land and fodder. Single cell protein is microbial biomass (algae such as Spirulina, bacteria such as Methylophilus methylotrophus, yeasts and fungi) grown on cheap materials like potato-processing waste, straw, molasses, animal manure or sewage. Microbes double their mass in hours, are rich in protein, minerals, fats and vitamins, and help reduce pollution by using wastes.

body.en: Because plant cells are totipotent, a small piece of a plant (an explant) grown aseptically on a nutrient medium (sugar, salts, vitamins, amino acids and growth regulators such as auxins and cytokinins) can regenerate whole plants. Micropropagation produces thousands of genetically identical plants (somaclones) quickly; it is used for tomato, banana and apple. Meristem culture gives virus-free plants. In somatic hybridisation, cell walls are digested to give protoplasts, protoplasts of two plants are fused, and the hybrid is grown into a plant, such as the pomato.

points.en: Meristem culture: virus-free; protoplast fusion: somatic hybrids

say.en: A small explant is sterilised and placed on a medium with auxin and cytokinin.
It forms an undifferentiated mass, the callus, and then shoots and roots.
Plantlets are hardened and moved to soil: thousands of identical plants.

caption.en: Optional: every cell of a micropropagated plant comes from mitosis, so all the plantlets are genetically identical to the explant.

problem.en: A banana grower needs 10 000 disease-free, uniform plants within months. Which method should be used, and from which part of the plant?

steps.en: Micropropagation gives thousands of identical plants quickly.
Using the meristem (shoot tip) as the explant gives virus-free plants.
So: meristem culture followed by micropropagation.

body.en: 10 doublings ≈ ×1000 (2¹⁰ = 1024). A microbe doubling every 2 h multiplies about a thousand times in 20 h.
